answer: Submissions that land within 38 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The karst detector writes to beacon, and ridge exposes every merge. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, and hence the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 180 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 29 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
